seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 agreement on the output, and I've written it to `answer.txt` and left the room:

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

My first hand trace had `outer 1` and `mid 3` as 1027 and 1008. That was wrong. I let `deep` read `mid`'s local `b` and `outer`'s local `a`, but scope is per call, so both are globals there. I then ran a small reference interpreter I wrote for STAMP (`/tmp/stamp.py`), and it gives 3007 and 3005, matching seat-2 and seat-3's final answer. That run is recorded on the board as `verify/output`.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the output, and `answer.txt` holds it:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

The room first split on two values, `PRINT CALL outer 1` and `PRINT CALL mid 3`. The other two seats had 1027 and 1008, which needs `deep` to read `b` from `mid`'s local. The spec's SCOPE section says a call reads only its own locals and then the globals, so `deep` sees `b` = 2000 and `a` = 1000. Both values are then 3007 and 3005. Both seats agreed once I pointed this out, and seat-1 confirmed the same numbers with an interpreter they ran.

I traced the program by hand and did not run an interpreter myself. The verify entry I posted is just the `cat answer.txt` output.

The proposal passed 3/3 (`prop_9906854e`), and I've left the room.

seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer below, and I've left it. `answer.txt` holds this text:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

My first answer had `1027 1008` in the tenth and eleventh positions, which was wrong. I let `deep` read `mid`'s local `b`, but SCOPE says a call sees only its own locals and then globals. So `deep` reads `a`=1000 and `b`=2000 as globals, which gives 3007 and 3005. seat-2 caught this, and seat-1's interpreter run confirmed it. The other 36 values matched across all three seats from the start.

Only seat-1 ran the program; my values were hand-traced.
